identity.title: Detecting the halo heating from AGN feedback with ALMA
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyse an archival ALMA band 4 observation of the most powerful radio-quiet quasar known (HE0515-4414)

evidence.quote: with the phase centred at the location of the quasar (RA = 05:17:07.63, Dec = -44.10.55.5)

question.value: Can the SZ decrement from AGN-heated halo gas around quasar HE0515-4414 be detected in the ALMA visibility plane after subtracting compact positive sources?

evidence.quote: We use a deep ALMA observation of HE0515-4414 in band 4, the most luminous quasar known at the peak of cosmic star formation (z=1.7), to search for the SZ signal tracing the heating of the galaxy’s halo.
Project code: 2016.1.00309.S, PI M.Lacy
HE0515-4414 was observed during ALMA cycle 4 in band 4 using the 12m array

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs centred at 133, 135, 145, 147 GHz, 128 channels each, 2 GHz each, 8 GHz total

evidence.quote: The SPWs are centred at 133, 135, 145 and 147 GHz, each with 128 channels covering a 2 GHz band.
a minimum baseline length of 15m and maximum of 384m
producing a synthesised beam with size 3.2$\times$2.3 arcsec$^{2}$
an RMS noise level of 3.8 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ is reached
with a total on-source time of 11.6 hours
The quasar was observed between January and March 2017 across 14 execution blocks

what.value: FABLE simulation SZ y-parameter maps and halo properties of a similar object

evidence.quote: we use the results of the FABLE simulations (Feedback Acting on Baryons in Large-scale Environments) (cite: Henden2018) to simulate observations of the SZ emission with ALMA.

what.value: Black hole mass of HE0515-4414 ~4.3e10 Msun

evidence.quote: ${M}_{BH}\approx4.3\times{10}^{10}{M}_{\odot}$ (cite: Lacy2018)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: FABLE SZ map of a similar object (M_BH 2.0e10 Msun, z=1.4) observed with CASA simobserve, 10 h, config C40-1

evidence.quote: We simulate observations of the object using the CASA task *simobserve* with 10 hours of on-source time and the same spectral setup as in the real observation.
The data were calibrated using the ALMA pipeline in CASA 4.7.2
The data were calibrated using the ALMA pipeline in CASA 4.7.2
J0519-4546 was used as the phase calibrator, and J0538-4405 and Mars were used as flux calibrators.
The calibration yields an absolute flux uncertainty of $\sim$5 per cent at the observed frequency
we have also produced an image of the continuum emission using the CASA task *tclean* with the the Högbom deconvolving algorithm
We also chose to use a single Taylor coefficient in the spectral model
A natural weighting was employed to maximise the sensitivity

method.value: Channel/time average to 30 s, then tclean natural weighting to identify five sources

evidence.quote: Five sources are observed with SNR larger than three, with the central emission coming from HE0515-4414.

method.value: Compute weights as reciprocal variance in uvdist bins; default weights ~2x too large, rescaled

evidence.quote: On average, the default ALMA weights are roughly twice as large as the statistically correct weights.

analysis_steps.goal: fit positive-emission sources in uv plane

method.value: Fit 3 symmetric Gaussians (A,B,C) and 2 point sources (D,E) to visibilities

evidence.quote: We therefore use a brightness model with the three resolved sources described as extended Gaussian profiles and the remaining two sources as point sources.

fitting.value: Bayesian MCMC sampler; median and 16th/84th percentiles of posteriors

evidence.quote: GALARIO allows users to choose the fitting procedure - in our case, a Bayesian MCMC sampler.

method.value: Subtract model from visibilities; bin residuals in 1 klambda bins; tclean residual images

evidence.quote: The residuals were found by subtracting the model presented in Fig. 4 from the observed visibilities.

validation.value: Checked >50 uv tracks and >20 antenna pairs in shortest bin

evidence.quote: We plotted the uv coordinates of the visibilities inside that bin and observed over 50 uv-tracks.

method.value: Reduced chi2 of shortest-baseline bin and chi2 CDF probability converted to sigma

evidence.quote: We find a 99.960 per cent probability of a ${\chi}_{red}^{2}$ smaller than the smallest baseline bin ${\chi}_{red}^{2}$, corresponding to a 3.35 $\sigma$ detection.

method.value: simobserve of FABLE SZ map, same pipeline; derive correction factor 2.5

evidence.quote: This suggests a total SZ flux of 0.5 mJy from HE0515-4414 after correcting for the primary beam attenuation and the flux resolved out by the array (i.e. a correction factor of 2.5).
The data were calibrated using the ALMA pipeline in CASA 4.7.2

used_for.value: Fitting visibility models of positive sources via MCMC

evidence.quote: GALARIO (cite: Tazzari2017) is a new code that makes use of GPUs and multiple CPU cores to compute synthetic visibilities quickly.
The significance of the SZ detection is 3.35$\sigma$.
We report a SZ flux of $\sim$ 0.2 mJy
$\sim$ 0.5 mJy after applying a correction factor
In our analysis this feature has a slightly lower significance, 3.2$\sigma$.
an RMS noise level of 3.8 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ is reached

findings_qualitative.value: Band 3 and ACA observations are predicted to detect SZ more effectively; ~40 h band 4 or ~10 h band 3 needed

evidence.quote: a total of $\sim$40 hours and $\sim$10 hours of on-source time are required for a clear detection in bands 4 and 3 respectively.

claims.hypothesis: SZ decrement from halo heating is detectable at short baselines
claims.experiment: GALARIO source subtraction and residual visibility analysis
claims.result: Negative residual at 5-6 klambda, chi2red~12, 3.35 sigma, ~0.2 mJy
claims.finding: Marginal SZ detection on ~300 kpc scales

evidence.quote: We obtain a marginal S-Z detection ($\sim$3.3$\sigma$) on scales of about 300 kpc
We show that our result is consistent with a simulated ALMA observation of a similar quasar in the FABLE cosmological simulations.

claims.hypothesis: Band 3 is better for SZ detection

evidence.quote: We, therefore, conclude that band 3 is twice as sensitive to the extended signal as band 4

why_this_method.value: Visibility-plane fitting gives direct uncertainties and separates compact from extended emission

evidence.quote: Working in the visibility plane (i.e. fitting the visibilities) is a straightforward operation on the interferometric measurements which allows a direct computation of uncertainties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct fit of a broad negative Gaussian for SZ was unsuccessful

evidence.quote: We attempted to directly model the SZ absorption by fitting a negative, very broad Gaussian. Unfortunately, this modelling does not provide well constrained results

limitations_admitted.value: Only dof=1 for short baselines; limited SNR prevents 2D fitting

evidence.quote: Our positive emission model, however, has 17 parameters, leaving dof=1.

Correction factor depends on a single FABLE object

Shortest bin may be affected by missing short-spacing coverage
